sentence: This project tests in rodents how general anesthetics may cause neurobehavioral deficits in offspring and looks for blood-based biomarkers of these effects.
This project provides researchers with tools to study glycan structures and the recognition of glycans by glycan-binding proteins.
This project studies how too much of one protein affects chondrogenesis in ischemic fractures and tests a targeted treatment to improve their repair.
This project tries to find out what influences substance use in young adult cancer survivors, using interviews and brief daily assessments.
This project studies the molecular causes of Barrett's esophagus and the related esophageal malignancy.
This project studies how the excitatory inputs onto parvalbumin-expressing inhibitory interneurons are regulated after chronic changes in circuit activity.
This project studies how impulsivity is linked to alcohol-related negative consequences in the daily life of young adults.
This project uses neuroimaging to test whether autistic individuals react strongly in brain networks for emotion but cannot recruit the mechanisms that regulate those reactions.
This project builds a model of NUT carcinoma, an aggressive cancer, from human pluripotent stem cells.
This project uses cryo-electron microscopy to watch viral particles during infection and learn which steps limit gene delivery to the nucleus.
This project tests whether a test that uses machine learning to combine age, vital signs and neurological examination detects large vessel occlusion stroke better.
This project uses AI to build decision support tools that help clinicians treat patients with cancer and other diseases.
This project looks for mechanisms that work together to drive growth of NUT carcinoma, an aggressive cancer, while blocking differentiation.
This project builds real-world evidence about medical devices using real-world data and develops active surveillance of device safety.
This project provides histology, imaging and digital pathology to study digestive and liver diseases in experimental animal models and humans.
This project offers flow cytometry that sorts and analyzes distinct cell populations for cancer research.
This project upgrades the gradient hardware of an MRI scanner to study how the brain works and neuropsychiatric and neurodegenerative disorders.
This project provides molecular technologies and data analysis support for environmental health research, including multi-omics studies.
This project studies Drosophila to learn how genetic novelties evolve and how adaptive gene expression varies.
This project studies how DNA-inspired Janus base biomaterials interact with cells and tissues and develops them to deliver mRNA into cells.
